title: Particulate nature of matter
competency: Demonstrate that matter is made up of tiny particles that are always moving.

keywords.def: A tiny piece of matter, too small to be seen.
The idea that matter is made up of tiny particles.

ideas.name: Matter is made of tiny moving particles

en.text: All matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them. The particles are too small to see. They are always moving. A balloon keeps its shape because gas particles fill it. Wind moving leaves and dust shows that particles move.

screens.title: Inside a balloon
screens.ask: You blow up a balloon. What fills it and keeps its round shape?
opts: Tiny gas particles we cannot see
screens.after: The balloon is full of tiny gas particles. We cannot see them, but they push on the rubber.
screens.best: Tiny gas particles we cannot see

screens.title: 2.1.2 Particulate nature of matter
paras: The particle model says all matter is made of tiny, moving particles.
There are spaces between the particles.
The particles are too small to be seen.

screens.title: What the activity shows
paras: An inflated balloon is filled with small particles of gas.
The gas may be helium, hydrogen, oxygen or air.
Wind blows leaves and dust around.
This shows particles of matter are in continuous motion.
The idea that matter is made of tiny particles is the particulate nature of matter.

screens.title: Evidence for tiny moving particles
screens.ask: Tap each one. What does it show?
items: Gas particles fill it and push on the rubber. So it keeps its round shape.
It may be helium, hydrogen, oxygen or air. Each is made of tiny particles.
Moving air pushes leaves and dust around. Particles are in continuous motion.
Ice particles vibrate in place. Water particles slide past each other.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A tiny piece of matter, too small to be seen.
The idea that matter is made up of tiny particles.

screens.text: Particulate nature: what is matter made of?
opts: Tiny particles that are always moving
screens.ans: Tiny particles that are always moving
screens.why:
The particle model says all matter is made of tiny particles.
The particles are always moving, with spaces between them.
The balloon shows gas particles filling it. Moving dust shows motion.
So matter is tiny particles that are always moving.
"One big solid piece" is wrong: even a stone is made of particles.
screens.clue: Think about the balloon and the moving dust.

screens.ask: Fill in the particle idea: everything is made of ___.
screens.why:
The particle model starts with one idea.
All matter, solid, liquid or gas, is built from tiny pieces.
Those tiny pieces are called particles.
Answer: particles.
screens.clue: Choose from the word box: particles, moving, energy …

screens.ask: Fill in the particle idea: particles are always ___.
screens.why:
Wind blows dust and leaves around.
A smell spreads across a room.
Both show that particles never stop.
Answer: moving.
screens.clue: Think of dust in the wind.

screens.text: Heat and particles: the particles in hot water have ___ energy than particles in cold water.
screens.why:
Hot water was heated. Heat is a form of energy.
So the hot-water particles received more energy.
More energy makes particles move faster.
Answer: more.

screens.text: True or false: the particles in ice move less than the particles in liquid water.
screens.why:
Ice is a solid. Its particles only vibrate in place.
Liquid water flows. Its particles slide past each other.
Sliding is more movement than vibrating.
So the statement is true.

screens.text: Particles in motion: a drop of perfume is opened in a corner. Soon the whole room smells. Which idea explains this best?
opts: Perfume particles move and spread out
The smell is a form of light
screens.ans: Perfume particles move and spread out
screens.why:
Step 1: perfume is matter, made of tiny particles.
Step 2: particles are always moving.
Step 3: the moving particles spread through the air of the room.
So the smell reaches every corner.
"Particles stay still" cannot explain a smell far from the bottle.

items.ask: Use the word box. Everything is made of ___.
items.why:
The particle model: all matter is made of tiny pieces.
The word box name for these pieces is "particles".
Answer: particles.
items.clue: Word box: increase, less, faster, cold, temperature, water, particles, moving, more, energy.

items.ask: Use the word box. Particles are always ___.
items.why:
Particles never stop: think of dust in the wind.
The word box word for this is "moving".
Answer: moving.

items.ask: Use the word box. An increase in energy makes particles move ___.
items.why:
Heating gives particles more energy.
With more energy they move more quickly.
The word box word is "faster".
Answer: faster.

items.ask: Use the word box. An increase in ___ is the same thing as an increase in energy.
items.why:
Heating a substance raises its temperature.
Heating also gives its particles more energy.
So a rise in temperature is a rise in energy.
Answer: temperature.

items.ask: Use the word box. The particles in hot water have more energy than ___ water.
items.why:
Hot water has been heated; cold water has not.
So hot-water particles have more energy than cold-water particles.
Answer: cold.

items.ask: Use the word box. The particles in ice move ___ than particles in water.
items.why:
Ice is solid: its particles only vibrate in place.
Water particles slide past each other.
So ice particles move less.
Answer: less.

test.text: True or false: matter is made up of tiny particles that are too small to be seen.
test.why:
This is the particulate nature of matter.
All matter is made of tiny particles.
They are far too small to see with our eyes.
So the statement is true.

test.text: Particle evidence: why does an inflated balloon keep its shape?
opts: It is filled with gas particles
test.ans: It is filled with gas particles
test.why:
Blowing puts gas into the balloon.
The gas is made of tiny moving particles.
They push on the rubber from inside.
So the balloon stays round because it is filled with gas particles.
"It is empty" is wrong: let the gas out and it goes flat.

test.text: Particle evidence: wind blows dust around. What does this show?
opts: Particles of matter are always moving
test.ans: Particles of matter are always moving
test.why:
Dust and air are matter made of particles.
Wind is moving air. It pushes the dust along.
The book uses this to show continuous motion.
Answer: particles of matter are always moving.

test.ask: Energy and motion: an increase in energy makes particles move ___.
test.why:
Energy is what makes particles move.
More energy means more movement.
So the particles move faster.
Answer: faster.

test.text: Heating and particles: Kebede heats water from 20 °C to 60 °C. What happens to its particles?
test.why:
Step 1: heating from 20 °C to 60 °C adds energy.
Step 2: more energy makes particles move faster.
Step 3: the particles do not grow or vanish; they only speed up.
Answer: they move faster.

notes.text: Activity 2.3 keeps the book's word box. For blank 3 the word "energy" is in the question so each word is used once.
